node-1.label: Painful swelling over the right lower leg for 1 week

node-2.label: A woman in her 70s with a history of recurrent stasis dermatitis treated with long-term topical and systemic corticosteroids

node-3.label: She recalled being traumatized by plants on her right lower leg 3 months before presentation; she grows plants, especially orchids, inside her bedroom and on the balcony

node-4.label: Physical examination showed necrotic ulcers covered by hemorrhagic crusts and purulent debris on the right lower leg; she was afebrile

why.why: Laboratory and pathology analyses now show angioinvasive septate hyphae in vessel lumens and culture-confirmed filamentous fungus with appressoria, in a patient with plant trauma and corticosteroid immunosuppression. This establishes post-trauma skin infection as the leading diagnosis and explains the necrotic purulent ulcer. Confidence is raised from 0.45 to 0.85; mixed bacterial infection or deep extension cannot be fully excluded because bacterial culture and deep imaging were not obtained.

Although recurrent stasis dermatitis and the lower-leg location initially suggested infected venous stasis ulcer, biopsy and culture demonstrate a primary angioinvasive fungal infection linked to plant trauma and immunosuppression. This makes infected venous stasis ulcer less likely as the primary explanation, though stasis dermatitis may remain a background predisposing factor.

Histological examination shows no malignancy, and the necrotic/purulent ulcer is fully explained by angioinvasive fungal infection with septate hyphae in vessel lumens. The recent plant trauma and positive fungal culture further argue against malignant transformation as the primary cause, so confidence is lowered from 0.15 to 0.05.

Histology demonstrates fungal hyphae and vascular necrosis rather than a primary inflammatory/vasculitic process, and the purulent necrotic findings are attributable to fungal infection. Therefore inflammatory skin ulcer is not supported; confidence is lowered from 0.10 to 0.05.

node-10.label: Fungal culture confirms a filamentous fungus with appressoria and high ITS similarity

node-11.label: PAS stain shows abundant thin-walled septate hyphae; Fontana-Masson stain is negative for melanin

node-12.label: Histological examination shows no evidence of malignancy

node-13.label: Post-traumatic angioinvasive fungal infection of the right lower leg

why.why: The laboratory physician and radiologist independently reaffirm that biopsy and culture evidence—angioinvasive septate hyphae with necrotic vessel occlusion, PAS-confirmed hyphae in vessel lumens, Fontana-Masson negativity ruling out pigmented fungi, and culture with appressoria plus ITS sequence identification—establish post-traumatic angioinvasive fungal infection. Combined with plant trauma and corticosteroid immunosuppression, this explains the painful necrotic purulent ulcer. Confidence remains 0.85 because bacterial culture and lower-extremity MRI/CT were not performed, so secondary bacterial co-infection and deep extension cannot be fully excluded.
